subject: SOC 2 Type II report request and onboarding evidence — next steps

To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Subject: SOC 2 Type II report request for onboarding

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of our procurement and security review we'd like to collect Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II report and any supporting materials you can share (bridge letter, scope confirmation, evidence index). Our security team needs:

- SOC 2 Type II report covering the past 12 months (testing period dates)
- A bridge letter if governance controls have materially changed since the last report
- A short evidence checklist or index mapping controls to artifacts (logs, configs, policies)
- Guidance for secure transfer of any sensitive artifacts

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated ETA? Also please let me know the exact audit period dates included in the report — our contract team needs that to finalize the data retention clause.

Appreciate it — looking to close the security review this week if possible.

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe
Security Programs Manager
Acme Corp

--

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report request for onboarding

Hi Jane — thanks for outlining the request. Quick summary of what we can share today and next steps: 

1) What we can share now (attached/links):
   - Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025_Report.pdf (official Type II report covering 2024-11-01 to 2025-10-31)
   - SOC2_bridge_letter_template.docx (we can sign/issue a signed bridge letter if the report period doesn't cover your required dates)
   - evidence_request_checklist.xlsx (mapping of control families to representative artifacts)

2) Common clarifications:
   - Audit period: our latest Type II report covers 2024-11-01 through 2025-10-31 (testing period). If you require coverage up to contract start in 2026, we'd provide a bridge letter that documents any material control changes and indicates the interim controls in place.
   - Narrow requests: If your team requires particular artifacts (e.g., raw CloudTrail exports, full config snapshots), we prefer to provide representative artifacts and an index — raw logs can be large and often exchanged via SFTP or a secure SharePoint link under an NDA.

3) Secure transfer options (pick one):
   - Secure Drive link (view + download) — link will be time-limited and access-controlled.
   - SFTP drop (sftp.redwood.example:/incoming/acme/) — we will provide account and instructions.
   - Encrypted ZIP (PGP) sent via encrypted email transfer for small bundles.

4) ETA: I can share the report and the checklist within a couple hours. If you confirm the transfer method we will stage the bridge letter template for legal to sign (if needed) and prepare representative artifacts within 2 business days.

I've attached the report and the checklist to this email for your security team's review. Marcus is looped in to coordinate artifact delivery; Neha will assist on legal/bridge letter execution if required.

Next steps: Please reply with preferred transfer method and whether you need the bridge letter signed prior to contract start.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025_Report.pdf (pdf, 3.2MB); evidence_request_checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)

Thanks Vivek — that timeline works. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Can you confirm whether the SOC 2 report's scope includes production inference workloads (in particular, model serving endpoints and the KV cache layer)? We need scope alignment for our SaaS security posture.
2) For the bridge letter: our procurement team asks that any bridge letter explicitly state the controls that are out of scope or materially changed and the date through which the bridge letter attests coverage. Is that something your legal can provide?

Transfer method: SFTP drop is preferred due to file sizes. Also please include a short README that maps filenames to control IDs so our reviewers can quickly locate artifacts.

Appreciate the quick turn — if you can get the bridge letter template now that would speed things up.

Best,
Jane
